newsitem.title: SPAIN: Argentaria agrees with unions on 2,100 job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Argentaria agrees with unions on 2,100 job cuts.

text.p: Spanish bank Argentaria said on Thursday it and trade unions Workers Commission (CCOO) and General Trade Union (UGT) had agreed on a plan to cut 2,100 positions at its Bex unit.
In a statement, they said the plan forecasts early retirement for 1,500 workers at 85 percent of regular wages, with an additional 600 workers to take other early retirement by the year 2000.
They said the current staff of 6,600 will thereby be reduced by 2,100 to 4,500.
The entire Banco Exterior de Espana group, which includes national and foreign units, currently has 8,218 workers.
The deal affects workers 53 years old or older, who will get 85 percent of their wage for the next seven years. When they turn 60 they will get pensions for 90 percent of wages.
Workers who are at least 51 are allowed to participate in the plan at a level of 70 percent of full wages until they will turn 53.
For the next three years Bex will also implement staff reductions for additional 600 workers.
The expenditures for the plan are expected to be financed by Bex's shareholder funds which stand above 50 billion pesetas, the statement said.
Argentaria and unions also agreed on a collective agreement with pay rises of 3.25 percent for 1996 and of two percent for 1997 and 1998.
In May, Bex presented its plan for the reduction of 2,100 workers over three years.
